easy.def: A small tool or machine that does a special job.
examples: The gadget opens cans.
Dad has a new gadget.
I like this gadget.

more.def: A small tool or machine that does a particular job, and is often clever or new.
examples: Dad bought a gadget that slices apples.
The kitchen drawer is full of little gadgets.
She loves any new gadget that makes work easier.

easy.def: A joke.
examples: He told a funny gag.
The gag made us laugh.
That is an old gag.

more.def: A joke or a funny trick, especially in a show.
examples: The clown told a funny gag.
The movie had many silly gags.
The old gag still made us laugh.

easy.def: To get more of something.
examples: I gained a pound.
She gained a new friend.
The plant gains height each week.

more.def: To get something you did not have, or to get more of something.
examples: The team gained speed as it ran downhill.
He gained a new friend at camp.
The puppy gained weight and grew bigger.

easy.def: A huge group of stars.
examples: Our galaxy has many stars.
The galaxy is big.
The galaxy is far away.

more.def: A giant group of stars, gas and dust held together in space.
examples: Our galaxy is called the Milky Way.
A galaxy can contain billions of stars.
The galaxy looked like a swirl of light.

easy.def: Brave, noble and polite.
examples: The gallant knight helped the lady.
A gallant hero.
He was gallant.

more.def: Brave, kind and polite, especially in old stories.
examples: The gallant knight helped the lady across the stream.
In the story, a gallant hero saved the town.
He made a gallant offer to carry her bags.

easy.def: A place where art is shown.
examples: We went to an art gallery.
The gallery has paintings.
The gallery is open today.

more.def: A room or building where paintings and other art are shown.
examples: We went to an art gallery on Saturday.
The gallery has paintings by local artists.
The photo gallery is down the hall.

easy.def: A big unit for measuring liquid.
examples: I bought a gallon of milk.
The jug holds a gallon.
A gallon is big.

more.def: A unit for measuring liquid, equal to four quarts.
examples: The tank holds ten gallons of water.
The jug holds one gallon of water.
A gallon is four quarts.

easy.def: Something you play with rules.
examples: Let us play a game.
I like this game.
We won the game.

more.def: An activity with rules that people play for fun or to win.
examples: We played a board game when it rained.
Our soccer game starts at ten o'clock on Saturday.
Hide-and-seek is a game that needs a lot of space.

related.def: A person who plays games, often video games.

easy.def: Playing video games.
examples: He likes gaming.
Gaming is fun.
We spend time gaming.

more.def: The activity of playing video games on a computer, a console or a phone.
examples: My brother likes gaming and plays with his friends online.
The family limits the time we spend gaming on school nights.
The gaming club meets after school on Fridays.

easy.def: A group of friends.
examples: A gang of kids played.
The gang rode bikes.
A gang of ducks swam by.

more.def: A group of friends or people who go around together.
examples: A gang of kids played ball at the park.
The whole gang came to my party.
A gang of crows sat on the fence.

easy.def: An empty space.
examples: There is a gap in the fence.
A gap in my teeth.
The gap is wide.

more.def: An empty space or a break between two things.
examples: A gap opened in the clouds.
A gap in her teeth showed when she smiled.
Mind the gap between the train and the platform.

easy.def: To stare with your mouth open.
examples: The kids gaped.
She gaped at the huge cake.
He gaped in surprise.

more.def: To stare with your mouth wide open in surprise.
examples: The kids gaped at the giant dinosaur.
Tourists gaped at the tall mountain.
He gaped in surprise when the lights came on.

easy.def: A place where you park a car.
examples: Dad parked the car in the garage.
Our bikes are in the garage.
The garage door is open.

more.def: A building or part of a house for keeping a car, or a place where cars are fixed.
examples: We keep the ladder and the tools in the garage.
The mechanic at the garage fixed our brakes.
The rain stopped, so we rolled the bikes out of the garage.

easy.def: Things you throw away.
examples: Put the garbage in the can.
The garbage truck came.
I took out the garbage.

more.def: Waste that has been thrown away, such as old food and empty boxes.
examples: The garbage is collected every Tuesday.
He tossed the banana peel into the garbage.
The raccoon tipped over the garbage can.

easy.def: A place where plants grow.
examples: We have a garden.
The garden has flowers.
I water the garden.

more.def: A piece of ground where flowers, vegetables or other plants are grown.
examples: We grow tomatoes in our garden.
Bees buzzed around the flower garden.
The school garden has carrots and beans.

easy.def: A person who grows plants and flowers.
examples: The gardener watered the roses.
My grandpa is a gardener.
The gardener planted seeds.

more.def: A person who works in a garden or grows plants, as a job or for fun.
examples: The gardener pulled the weeds from the bed of tulips.
My aunt is a happy gardener who grows tomatoes every summer.
The park hired a gardener to look after the flower beds.

easy.def: Growing flowers and plants in a garden.
examples: Gardening is fun.
I like gardening.
We do gardening on Saturday.

more.def: The activity of growing and taking care of flowers, vegetables and other plants.
examples: Gardening is a good way to spend a sunny afternoon.
Grandpa loves gardening and grows tomatoes and beans.
We learned about gardening and planted seeds at school.

easy.def: A plant with a strong smell used in cooking.
examples: The garlic smells strong.
Mom added garlic.
The garlic bulb has cloves.

more.def: A plant with a strong smell and taste that is used to flavor food.
examples: Mom added garlic to the sauce.
The garlic smelled strong.
Garlic bread is my favorite.

easy.def: A piece of clothing.
examples: A coat is a garment.
The garment is warm.
She sewed a garment.

more.def: A piece of clothing, such as a coat, a shirt or a dress.
examples: A coat is a garment that keeps you warm in winter.
The tailor sewed the garment by hand.
Each garment in the shop had a price tag.

easy.def: Something like air that is not liquid or solid.
examples: Air is a gas.
Gas fills the balloon.
Steam is a gas.

more.def: A substance, such as air, that is not a solid or a liquid and can spread out.
examples: Helium is a gas that makes balloons float.
Water turns into a gas when it boils.
Oxygen is a gas that we breathe.

easy.def: Fuel for cars.
examples: Dad filled the car with gas.
The car needs gas.
Gas is expensive.

more.def: A liquid fuel for cars, short for gasoline.
examples: Dad stopped to buy gas.
The truck ran out of gas.
The price of gas went up.

easy.def: The liquid fuel that makes cars go.
examples: The car needs gasoline.
Gasoline is a fuel.
We bought gasoline.

more.def: A liquid fuel that is burned in the engines of cars and trucks.
examples: The car needed gasoline.
Gasoline is made from oil.
Dad filled the tank with gasoline.

easy.def: To breathe in suddenly because you are surprised.
examples: I gasped.
She gasped in surprise.
The crowd gasped.

more.def: To take a quick breath in because you are surprised or out of breath.
examples: She gasped when she saw the big surprise.
The runner gasped for air at the finish line.
The crowd gasped as the juggler dropped a ball.

easy.def: A door in a fence or wall.
examples: Close the gate.
The gate is open.
The dog went through the gate.

more.def: A part of a fence or wall that opens and closes like a door.
examples: Please close the gate behind you.
The horses ran out of the open gate.
We waited at the gate for our plane.

easy.def: An opening in a wall or fence that you go through.
examples: We walked through the gateway.
A stone gateway.
The gateway was open.

more.def: An opening in a wall or fence where a gate is, or a way into something bigger.
examples: We walked through the stone gateway into the old garden.
The city is the gateway to the mountains.
Reading is a gateway to new ideas.

easy.def: To bring things or people together.
examples: We gather sticks for the fire.
We gather around the campfire.
Hens gather by the food.

more.def: To collect things into one place, or to come together as a group.
examples: The class gathered around the teacher to hear the story.
Squirrels gather nuts for the winter.
A crowd gathered to watch the street performer.

easy.def: A short name for an alligator.
examples: A gator swam in the swamp.
I saw a gator.
The gator has big teeth.

more.def: A short name for an alligator.
examples: A gator lay still on the bank of the swamp.
We saw a gator sunning itself on a log.
The gator slid quietly into the water.

easy.def: A tool that measures something.
examples: The gauge shows how much gas is left.
Look at the gauge.
The rain gauge was full.

more.def: A tool or dial that measures an amount, such as the fuel in a car, the air in a tire or the rain in a storm.
examples: The gauge on the dashboard showed that the car was almost out of gas.
We used a rain gauge to measure how much rain fell during the storm.
A pressure gauge told us the tire needed more air.

easy.def: To guess how much or how good something is.
examples: I try to gauge the distance.
She gauged the wind.
He gauged how deep it was.

more.def: To measure something or make a careful guess about how big, how far or how likely it is.
examples: He tried to gauge how far he would need to jump to cross the stream.
The teacher watched our faces to gauge whether we understood.
We gauged the depth of the pool by looking at the lines on the wall.

easy.def: A thin cloth used to cover a cut.
examples: The nurse put gauze on my knee.
Gauze is soft and white.
He wrapped gauze around his finger.

more.def: A very thin, light cloth, often used to cover a wound.
examples: The nurse covered the cut with clean gauze.
A roll of gauze is kept in the first aid kit.
The costume wings were made of thin white gauze.

easy.def: To look at something for a long time.
examples: I gaze at the stars.
She gazed out the window.
The cat gazed at the bird.

more.def: To look at something steadily and for a long time.
examples: I gazed at the stars on a clear night.
She gazed out the window at the falling snow.
The cat gazed at the bird outside.

easy.def: A long, steady look.
examples: The cat's gaze was steady.
She met his gaze.
His gaze fell on the toy.

more.def: A long, steady look.
examples: The cat's gaze followed the bird across the yard.
She met his gaze and smiled.
His gaze fell on the toy at the back of the shelf.

easy.def: A fast, graceful animal with curved horns.
examples: A gazelle ran.
The gazelle is fast.
We saw a gazelle.

more.def: A small, graceful, fast-running animal of Africa and Asia that has curved horns and leaps through the air.
examples: The gazelle leaped across the grassy plain.
A gazelle can run very fast to escape from danger.
A herd of gazelles grazed in the early morning.
